pr_title: Fix trim analyzer warning for inferred type arguments
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/86032.

This replaces the syntax-based logic with:
- ISymbol-based logic that looks at generic instantiations in parameter types, return types, and base/interface types
- IOperation-based logic that looks at invocations

The syntax-based logic used to also warn for the types of local variables, but `SymbolKind.Local` isn't supported for `RegisterSymbolAction`. Since this falls into the category of warnings that isn't strictly necessary (based on nativeaot logic which only warns on generic instantiations that can actually lead to code execution), I just left out local variables.

I'm slightly concerned that this could be missing some cases, but at least it works on our existing testcases.

There are two slight differences in warning locations, which I don't expect to cause issues for warning suppressions:
- For invocations, the warning location used to be the generic method name, without the argument list. Using the IOperation-based approach, we use the invocation's location that includes the argument list.
- For properties that use arrow syntax (`RequireMethods<TFields> Property => null`), the ISymbol-based approach warns on the underlying getter method, whose location seems to be the body of the accessor. We used to warn on the return type specifically, but I couldn't find a better way to get the location.

issue_context.title: Trim Analyzer doesn't handle annotations on inferred generic arguments
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @agocke, @sbomer, @vitek-karas See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
```C# public class TestType { [RequiresUnreferencedCode("Dangerous")] public void Dangerous() {} } public static void InvokeDangerous<[DynamicallyAccessedMembers(DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.PublicMethods)] T>(T instance) { typeof(T).GetMethod("Dangerous").Invoke(instance, Array.Empty

The reason for this bug is that we use the syntax nodes to detect generic parameter usage in the analyzed code. But the inferred usage will not show up in the syntax tree (since it's missing). Not sure what is the correct way to handle this in the analyzer. Maybe we can detect most cases during our method body pass where we will see the inferred symbol.
We could look for generic instantiations on invocations when we have an IOperation tree in hand.

> We could look for generic instantiations on invocations when we have an IOperation tree in hand.

That's what I was trying to say with my above comment, unfortunately I used the wrong terms :-(.
FYI you could *also* look at symbols using the semantic model, but I thought it might be easier to just use the IOperation visitor

review_comments: Good catch, this wasn't warning with the change. I added some tests and support for this.
